change_note: Batch 7: index-fund tracking and fees, two-front selloffs and AI free cash flow, synchronized chip setups.

sources.title: הגרף הזה סימן תחתית 7 פעמים מאז 2020. ועכשיו? (Did this graph signal a bottom?)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)

principles.text: When only about a fifth of S&P 500 members trade above their 50-day average, breadth is washed out. Since 2020 such readings often sat near bottoms, but real crises pushed it far lower, so treat it as a setup to confirm, not a buy signal.
An index near its high while most of its members sit below their averages means leadership is narrow. Narrow leadership is fragile and deserves lower conviction on broad bullish calls.
Earnings reactions follow guidance more than the beat. A profit beat paired with weak forward guidance can still sell off hard, so judge a report by what management expects next.
A fear reading on a sentiment gauge is context, not a trigger. Lean contrarian only when breadth, trend and sentiment line up, and say which one would prove the call wrong.
A sector jump on a geopolitical shock, such as energy on shipping-lane tension, says little about the wider market and tends to fade when the headline does.

sources.title: אפוקליפסת הריטל? הסוכן של מטא שמאיים על אמזון (Retail apocalypse: Meta's agent threatening Amazon)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)

principles.text: When software agents do the shopping, sponsored placements lose their audience. Revenue that depends on a human browsing a page is exposed to any shift toward agent-made purchases.
Agent-era screen, part one: does revenue rely on customers forgetting to cancel, or on friction that stops them switching? An agent that audits subscriptions and compares offers removes both.
Agent-era screen, part two: does profit hinge on paid placement, or is the business only a middleman between buyer and seller? Agents route around both and go straight to the supplier.
In a platform shift, the rails tend to win: whoever settles the payment or runs the compute gets paid whichever agent wins. Prefer picks-and-shovels exposure while the winner is unclear.
Early in a shift, people using AI to help them shop far outnumber agents actually completing purchases. Size a disruption thesis to measured adoption, not to the narrative.

sources.title: איך לעשות פי 12 תשואה בבורסה בצורה פשוטה - האם זה אפשרי? (A 12x market-return strategy?)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)

principles.text: Buying last year's single best performer looks spectacular in a backtest, but the edge comes from a handful of outlier years. Most years are average or worse, so the result is closer to luck than to a repeatable rule.
A strategy that beats the index in only about three years of five carries heavy psychological cost. Most people abandon it in the losing stretch, which is when it matters.
Turnover and taxes can erase a backtested edge. Yearly rotation that wins before tax can lose to the index after tax, while buying and holding lets compounding do the work.
A concentrated bet on one name is a lottery ticket, not a core holding. Judge any momentum rule by its median year, not its best one.

sources.title: 7 מניות, אותו גרף בדיוק: סוד מטריד לפני שבוע הדיווחים (7 stocks, the same chart before earnings)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)

principles.text: When unrelated stocks trace the same chart, a shared factor such as rates, risk appetite or retail flows is driving them, not company news. Treat them as one bet and expect them to break together.
The options-implied move is the bar for an earnings reaction. A result is only news if the stock moves beyond what was already priced in.
A stock that ran hard into its report has front-run the good news. It needs a beat plus better guidance just to hold, and a plain beat can still trigger selling.
For each name, know the one segment metric the market is watching, such as a customer mix or a payments volume line. That line moves the stock more than the headline beat.
A breakout from a long range sets a technical target, but the story has to keep up. Without fundamental confirmation, breakouts tend to fail back into the range.

sources.title: רעידת אדמה: 180 דוחות יזיזו את התיק שלכם (180 earnings reports will move your portfolio)
sources.author: YouTube channel (name not given in batch)

principles.text: A peak earnings week that also holds a central-bank decision piles up event risk. Avoid new high-conviction calls whose horizon spans that week unless the event is the thesis.
For companies that beat every quarter, a beat is already priced. Only the size of the beat or a change in guidance moves the stock.

For mega-cap tech in the AI build-out, capex guidance and cloud growth now move the stock more than EPS. Higher capex can dent near-term EPS without hurting the stock if cloud revenue confirms the spend.
A sleepy chart into earnings usually comes with a small implied move. Such names need a new narrative, not a routine beat, to re-rate.

sources.title: גוגל נשברת, פלנטיר פורצת — ומה קורה עם האג״ח 10? (Google breaks down, Palantir breaks out, and the 10-year)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: When the 10-year yield climbs toward what stocks are expected to earn, money rotates into risk-free paper. Rising long yields are a headwind, hardest on long-duration growth names.
Read why yields rise. Weak growth data plus hawkish signals and a poor auction is worse for stocks than yields rising on strong growth.
Know where inflation comes from. When it sits in business inputs such as memory and chips, the suppliers with pricing power gain and their customers' margins get squeezed.
A thin-volume zone below a broken level is an air pocket. If the level is not reclaimed, price can drop quickly to the next heavy-volume area, which makes that level a clean invalidation.
A breakout is confirmed by rising volume and by old resistance holding as support on the retest. Losing that level again invalidates it.
Fear readings while the index sits near its high signal anxiety beneath the surface. Check breadth and rates before trusting the index level.

sources.title: הטעות שכולם עושים כשהשוק בשיא — ואיך להימנע ממנה (The mistake everyone makes at market highs)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: All-time highs cluster. Strong years print many of them, so a new high is more often followed by more highs than by a crash.
Reluctance to buy at a high is psychology, not math. People waiting for a dip tend to hold out for a bigger one and end up buying back higher.
Historically, investing a lump sum at once beat holding cash for a better entry, partly because highs cluster. Long dry spells do happen, so horizon and diversification still matter.
Being near an all-time high is not, on its own, a reason for a bearish stance. A bearish call needs its own evidence.

sources.title: בנק אוף אמריקה קובע: המניה הזו עומדת להתחיל לעלות (Bank of America: this stock is about to rise)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: Compare a leader's forward P/E with the index's. When a fast grower trades at or below the market multiple, the price implies little growth, and the question becomes what would break.
Parabolic runs in cyclical sectors such as semiconductors often end in deep corrections. Size bullish conviction to how stretched the run is.
Several successful tests of a long moving average followed by a break of the downtrend line is a classic base. Resistance above still caps the first move.
When an industry repurposes its infrastructure for a new wave of demand, such as crypto miners hosting AI compute, new buyers and volume tend to show up before earnings do.
An analyst upgrade is an input, not a verdict. Record it as a dated claim and let scoring judge it.

sources.title: מאגניפיסנט 7 יוציאו את הבורסה מהתקיעות שלה? (Will the Magnificent 7 break the market out of its rut?)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: When the index goes sideways for weeks, check its largest members one by one. The next leg usually follows whichever group breaks first: leaders breaking down or laggards bouncing.
Classify each name by structure: higher highs and lows (healthy), a range (waiting for a breakout), or a broken uptrend in a falling channel (repair needed). Stance should follow structure.
A stock that has gone nowhere for years while swinging hard offers volatility, not trend. Keep conviction low until it leaves the range.
A broken name needs a higher high above a named level to reverse. Until then, rallies inside the channel are bounces, and that level is the natural invalidation for a bullish call.

sources.title: 13 ימים של ירוק ברצף — השוק חצה את הגבול? (13 green days in a row: did the market cross the line?)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: A long streak of up days that lifts the index far above its 20- and 50-day averages is stretched. Expect digestion, often a pullback, before the next leg.
Unfilled gaps below the price are often revisited. Treat them as likely pullback targets, not certainties.
Relief rallies on easing geopolitical risk can be fast and broad. Once that risk premium is gone, the next move needs earnings or data.
When retail chatter crowds into squeezes and speculative themes and sentiment reads greed, tighten risk instead of adding aggressive bullish calls.
The sector that bounces hardest after a selloff is often short covering first. Confirm follow-through before calling it new leadership.

sources.title: לפני שאתם קונים דירה — חובה לראות את זה (Before you buy an apartment)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: Sellers bound by loan covenants keep list prices sticky even when demand stalls, because an official cut would devalue the collateral. The real discount then shows up in terms and side deals, not in the headline price.
When lenders are carrying unsold inventory for leveraged sellers, bargaining power shifts to the buyer with cash. Official price indices lag that shift.

sources.title: הכסף הגדול חתך 92% ממייקרון — ומה הוא קנה במקום (Big money cut 92% of Micron, and what it bought instead)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: 13F filings show what large funds held at quarter end, published weeks later, with no reasons and no shorts or hedges. Treat them as delayed context on positioning, never as a live signal.

Heavy institutional selling of a cyclical leader after a strong run often signals profit taking ahead of a cycle turn. Check where the money went inside the same sector before reading it as bearish for the whole group.

sources.title: המדריך המעודכן לעונת הדיווחים - חלק 1 (The updated guide to earnings season, part 1)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: Read a report in order: guidance first, then revenue growth and its quality, then EPS. A beat built on cost cuts or a lower share count is weaker than one built on revenue.
Before a report, note the options-implied move. After it, ask whether the stock moved more or less than priced, and why. That gap is the market's real verdict.
Do not open a new short-horizon stance a day or two before a report unless the report is the thesis. The outcome becomes a coin flip on the event, not on the analysis.

sources.title: אנבידיה זולה יותר מ-S&P 500? השוק יודע משהו? וברודקום? (Is Nvidia cheaper than the S&P 500? And Broadcom?)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: A rising stock can get cheaper on forward P/E when earnings estimates climb faster than the price. Ask whether the discount reflects real growth or doubt that the estimates will hold.
A low forward multiple on a business with cyclical demand often means the market expects peak earnings. Watch the direction of estimate revisions, not just the multiple.
A second play in the same theme spreads company risk but not theme risk. Two chip names riding one AI build-out are largely the same bet.

sources.title: האנליסטים בטוחים ב-2026 – וזה בדיוק למה הם עלולים לטעות (Analysts are confident about 2026, which is why they may be wrong)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: Year-ahead bank outlooks describe consensus. When everyone shares one story, surprises tend to come from the other side, so use outlooks as a map of expectations, not as a forecast.
Let price confirm a thesis, through a breakout or a hold of support, instead of committing to a rigid twelve-month macro call.
In a two-speed, K-shaped economy, winners and losers split inside the same sector. Pick names, not just sectors.
AI's power demand ties tech to energy. Data-centre growth is also a utilities and power-supply story.

sources.title: לייב פתיחה יום שישי 2.10.26 (Live Friday open, 2 Oct 2026)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: Friday sessions with weekly options expiring are noisy. Do not read much into a Friday-open move without follow-through the next week.
A rapid-fire chart review produces setups, not theses. Each setup needs its own evidence and invalidation before it becomes a pick.

sources.title: עוקב או מחקה? איך דופקים אתכם בפנסיה על הסנפ 500 (Tracker or imitator? How pensions short-change you on the S&P 500)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: Same index label, different results. A passive track that copies the index with derivatives, futures or forced bond sleeves can trail it badly, so compare your track with the raw index over the same period.
Fees compound against you. A fraction of a percent a year over decades takes a large share of the final balance, so push fees toward the lowest available.
Currency conversion inside a foreign-index fund is a hidden cost. Ask how it is done and at what rate.
A cheap index inside an expensive wrapper is not cheap. Distribution commissions are often buried in the management fee of a passive product.

sources.title: הכל קורס - זה הסימן דווקא לקנות? (Everything is crashing: is this actually the signal to buy?)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: When stocks fall on two fronts at once, geopolitics and rising yields, the yield pressure usually outlasts the headlines. Watch the 10-year more than the news flow.
A volatility spike that is sold straight away signals confusion, not panic. Capitulation lows usually need fear that persists.

Heavy AI capex can turn free cash flow negative even when revenue is strong, and the market punishes that when the payback is unclear. For the big spenders, track free cash flow, not only revenue and EPS.
A market dominated by one industry can lead that industry. A breakout in the chip-heavy Korean index can foreshadow a move in global semiconductors.

sources.title: התבנית שחוזרת בהרבה מניות — עלייה או קריסה? (The pattern repeating in many stocks: surge or crash?)
sources.author: Micha (YouTube channel)

principles.text: When a whole group shows the same setup (a rally, a sharp drop, then a push at the falling trendline), treat it as one decision. The breakout tends to succeed or fail across the group together.
A breakout that starts far above its long averages has less fuel. Being stretched above the 150- and 200-day averages raises the odds of a retest first.
A famous short call often lands on stocks that were already technically stretched. The price was the warning before the headline.
Ahead of scheduled macro events such as jobs data or a central-bank symposium, a stretched index tends to stall. Avoid new short-horizon calls that hinge on the event.
